note: One entry per repository. Edit this file by pull request, or open a 'Suggest a repository' issue and it gets added for you. Descriptions are one sentence: what it is and why a functional consultant would care. No client material, ever.

categories.name: Control unit & harness
categories.blurb: The kit this site describes. Start here.

categories.name: AI tools & agent instructions
categories.blurb: How Claude, Copilot and the rest read instructions, and the servers that connect them to your systems.

categories.name: SAP — official
categories.blurb: Maintained by SAP. Style guides, samples, SDKs.

categories.name: SAP — community tooling
categories.blurb: Practitioner-built. The tools working teams actually use.

categories.name: Data, integration & standards
categories.blurb: The open formats and protocols the additive layer is built on.

categories.name: Templates & starters
categories.blurb: Copy these to start a repository that looks right on day one.

repos.name: EVEglyphDesign/canon
repos.description: One canon, many surfaces: edit one file and the Claude, Copilot and Perplexity versions are generated from it, with a check that fails when they drift.

repos.name: EVEglyphDesign/eve-glyph-boot-contract
repos.description: The operating contract behind the harness — read-before-search, spend classes, output rules — as a loadable Claude skill with a defect register and version arc.

repos.name: EVEglyphDesign/sovereign-starter
repos.description: A one-file starter you paste into any AI surface: standing rules in your own voice, an observation register, and the rule of three that turns observations into rules.

repos.name: EVEglyphDesign/sapfans-io
repos.description: This site. The tutorial, the usage standards, and this directory — clone it and everything here is yours.

repos.name: anthropics/claude-code
repos.description: Claude's terminal agent. Works inside a clone of your repository, reads CLAUDE.md automatically, and can write files rather than answers.

repos.name: anthropics/skills
repos.description: Anthropic's public skills — the SKILL.md format the harness uses, with worked examples for documents, spreadsheets and PDFs.

repos.name: github/awesome-copilot
repos.description: Community-contributed instructions, agents and skills for GitHub Copilot — the Copilot-side equivalent of a skills library.

repos.name: agentsmd/agents.md
repos.description: The AGENTS.md format: one vendor-neutral instruction file that Claude, Copilot and a growing set of other coding agents all read.

repos.name: modelcontextprotocol/servers
repos.description: Reference MCP servers — the protocol that lets an AI tool read your repository, your files or your database instead of guessing.

repos.name: github/github-mcp-server
repos.description: GitHub's official MCP server. Gives an AI tool read and write access to repositories, issues and pull requests with permissions you scope.

repos.name: cloudflare/mcp
repos.description: Cloudflare's full-API MCP server — DNS, zones, Workers — using a search-then-execute pattern that keeps the token cost small.

repos.name: SAP/styleguides
repos.description: SAP's own coding style guides, Clean ABAP above all. The reference to point at when a developer asks what 'done properly' means.

repos.name: SAP/abap-cleaner
repos.description: Applies a hundred-plus cleanup rules to ABAP at one keystroke. Useful to know exists when reviewing custom code quality on a programme.

repos.name: SAP/cloud-sdk-js
repos.description: SAP Cloud SDK for JavaScript — typed clients for S/4HANA Cloud, SuccessFactors and other SAP services over OData and OpenAPI.

repos.name: SAP-samples
repos.description: SAP's organisation of sample code — hundreds of small, runnable examples across BTP, integration, analytics and extension scenarios.

repos.name: abapGit/abapGit
repos.description: Git client for ABAP. The reason ABAP code can live in a GitHub repository at all — and be reviewed, versioned and shared like everything else.

repos.name: abaplint/abaplint
repos.description: Static analysis for ABAP that runs outside SAP — in CI, in an editor, or on a pull request.

repos.name: abap-openapi/abap-openapi
repos.description: Generates ABAP clients and servers from an OpenAPI description, so an integration contract can be written once and honoured on both sides.

repos.name: OAI/OpenAPI-Specification
repos.description: The OpenAPI standard itself. When an interface is described this way, every tool — including the AI ones — can read the contract.

repos.name: OData/odata.net
repos.description: Reference .NET libraries for OData, the query protocol most SAP read access uses. Useful for understanding what an OData feed can and cannot do.

repos.name: apache/iceberg
repos.description: An open table format for large analytical datasets. Where a mirrored record can land so that it loads anywhere, not just in the tool that wrote it.

repos.name: duckdb/duckdb
repos.description: An in-process SQL database that opens CSV, Parquet and Excel files directly. The fastest way for a functional analyst to query an extract without a server.

repos.name: eclipse-tractusx/tractusx-edc
repos.description: The Catena-X data-space connector — sovereign, contract-governed data sharing across an industrial supply chain. Same idea as the additive layer, applied between companies.

repos.name: github/gitignore
repos.description: The standard collection of .gitignore files. Pick the one for your tooling so exports, secrets and scratch files never end up committed.

repos.name: othneildrew/Best-README-Template
repos.description: A well-structured README template. A repository whose README says what it is, who it serves and its current state is one people actually use.

repos.name: EVEglyphDesign/sapfans-io — repo-skeleton
repos.description: The folder shape from the tutorial — README, decisions, analysis, sources, canon — ready to copy into a new repository.
